portInfo.description: Stockholm cruise ships use several Ports of Stockholm areas—commonly Stadsgården (close to Gamla Stan/Slussen) or Värtahamnen/Frihamnen farther northeast. Confirm your terminal: walking into Gamla Stan is realistic from Stadsgården, while Värtan calls usually need bus, taxi, or metro connections.
portInfo.location: Eastern Sweden on Lake Mälaren / Baltic approaches
portInfo.population: City roughly 1 million; metro area ~2.4 million

facts.established: Historic Baltic capital; modern cruise terminals across multiple inner-city harbors
facts.significance: Premier Baltic cruise capital and common overnight/turnaround port
culturalHighlights: Gamla Stan lanes and Royal Palace exteriors

size.portCapacity: Multiple cruise terminals across Ports of Stockholm harbors
size.annualVisitors: Leading Baltic cruise destination volumes (see Ports of Stockholm season reports)

climate.averageTemp: Mild summers; cold winters with short daylight
climate.rainySeason: Showers possible in summer; winter brings snow/ice risk
climate.humidity: Fresh Baltic air; evenings cool even in summer
climate.description: Peak cruise season is summer with long daylight for Gamla Stan and Djurgården. Shoulder months are quieter but cooler; winter daylight is limited.

politics.stability: Ordinary urban/tourist awareness applies; check local notices if demonstrations or large events affect transfer routes.
politics.visaRequirements: Sweden follows Schengen / European short-stay frameworks for many travelers, but visa and passport rules depend on nationality and can change. Confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID only where your cruise line and destination authorities explicitly accept it). Shore excursions do not change document rules—keep required ID with you ashore.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Identify Stadsgården vs Värtahamnen/Frihamnen before planning a walk. Ships publish terminal assignments in final documents.
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Stadsgården often ~1–2 km to Gamla Stan/Slussen; Värtan area roughly 4–6+ km to the old town
gettingThere.walkingTime: Stadsgården: frequently 15–30 minutes to Gamla Stan. Värtan: plan transit, not a casual walk—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Readily available; useful from Värtan with limited time
gettingThere.publicTransport: SL tickets cover buses, metro, and trams. From Värtan, bus/metro combinations reach T-Centralen and Gamla Stan
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Stadsgården often ~1–2 km to Gamla Stan/Slussen; Värtan area roughly 4–6+ km to the old town

thingsToDo.intro: Stadsgården can be walkable to Gamla Stan; Värtahamnen/Frihamnen usually need bus, metro, or taxi. Identify the terminal before planning a stroll.
topThings: Gamla Stan (Old Town) lanes and Stortorget: allow 75–90 minutes. Cobbles; keep valuables simple.
Vasa Museum (Djurgården): allow 90–120 minutes inside plus Djurgården transfer—ticket ahead when possible.
City Hall (Stadshuset) exterior / waterfront: allow 30–45 minutes.
ABBA The Museum / Djurgården cluster: only on longer calls with timed tickets.
Södermalm viewpoints (Stadsgården berths): allow 45–60 minutes local walk when alongside there.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: SL tickets cover buses/metro/trams. Do not assume every Stockholm berth is a Gamla Stan walk.
